subject: PoC test plan & network feasibility for FinOptima (private inference comparison)
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina@finoptima.com>, Tom Reed <tom.reed@finoptima.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Sep 2025 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: PoC test plan & network feasibility for FinOptima (private inference comparison)

Hi Lina / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our end + proposed next steps so we have a single place to track items before the PoC kickoff: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary driver: extractive summarization + PII-safe embeddings for regulatory reporting (low latency at 99th pctile, strict data residency).
- Preferred deployment: private VPC or on-prem air-gapped with a customer-managed control plane option.
- Main competitor comparisons: you mentioned evaluating AWS Bedrock (policy constraints on control plane traffic) and a proprietary managed inference API from VendorX.

Questions / constraints to confirm
1) Air-gap feasibility: you need a plan where the inference runtime can be completely isolated from internet egress during inference, and the control plane only accepts authenticated connections during scheduled maintenance windows.
2) KMS/Key custody: bring-your-own-key to HSM/KMS is a hard requirement.
3) Network topology: no outbound connections to third-party model registries; fallback routing to hosted models is allowed but must be opt-in.
4) Compliance: SOC 2 evidence and audit logs for token-level access.

Proposed next tests (attached PoC test plan) — high level
- Test A: Control-plane handshake with a restricted management subnet (validate canaries, auth, and offline lifecycle ops).
- Test B: Network blackout / air-gap exercise (runtime only: validate inference continues on local weights and KV cache).
- Test C: End-to-end latency sweep (50–3k token profiles) against our dedicated config vs. AWS/GCP endpoints you’re evaluating.
- Test D: Key rotation + HSM validation (rotate during live traffic window).

Attachments: FinOptima_PoC_TestPlan.xlsx (detailed timelines & tooling), redwood-network-topology-draft.png (proposed architecture).

Asks / next steps
- Can you confirm availability for a 60-min technical kickoff week of Sep 15 (we propose Thu 9–10am PT)?
- Please send your security contact for SOC2 evidence sharing and a point of contact for networking so we can pre-seed our network checklist.

I’ve looped in Ben (solutions) and Marissa (platform PM) to help run the tests and coordinate on the control-plane specifics.

Thanks — happy to adjust the plan based on what you want prioritized.

—
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 03 Sep 2025 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC test plan & network feasibility for FinOptima (private inference comparison)

Thanks Rachel — nice summary. Two quick clarifications I’ll add to the plan before the kickoff: 

1) Fallbacks: we can implement an opt-in fallthrough policy that routes to a Redwood-hosted model variant in another region if the private pool is saturated, but there are two knobs you’ll want: (a) explicit opt-in on a per-route basis, and (b) a circuit-breaker that prevents any egress during an air-gap test.

2) Benchmarks: I’ll attach our latency deck and a short script to run against the dedicated config vs. Bedrock so we get apples-to-apples numbers.

Link to internal runbook I referenced: https://redwood-internal.company/docs/private-deploy-runbook (read-only).

I’ll prep the artifacts and upload to the HubSpot record before the kickoff.

—Ben

Date: Mon, 08 Sep 2025 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC test plan & network feasibility for FinOptima (private inference comparison)

Rachel / Ben —

Appreciate the plan. A few clarifications from our security and procurement threads: 

- Procurement timeline: target contract signature by end of Oct. We need a short mutual action plan to show our legal and infra teams.
- SOC 2 / ISO: please share an evidence checklist. We’ll need runtime logs and change history for at least 12 months.
- Air-gap detail: when you say "air-gap exercise" we need a clear rollback plan if there’s a model drift or cache corruption after extended offline operation. Can Redwood support a manual fallback to a specific pinned model if needed?

Also, can you confirm whether any control-plane telemetry or agent in our network initiates outbound TLS connections to third-party registries during normal op? Our infra team flagged VendorX because their control plane requires periodic registry checks.

If we can get a one-page MA (mutual action) and the test plan updated with the rollback steps, we’ll share it with procurement and security.

Thanks,
Lina Morales
Director, Data Platforms
FinOptima
lina@finoptima.com
From: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
To: Lina Morales <lina@finoptima.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PoC test plan & network feasibility for FinOptima (private inference comparison)

Lina —

Great questions. Short answers and commits below, I’ll follow up with updated artifacts by EOD today.

- MA / timeline: attached (short one-pager) — roadmap to contract by Oct 31, with PoC execution weeks Sep 22–Oct 10.
- SOC2 evidence checklist: Ben will push the checklist + sample logs to the HubSpot file area. We can provide 12 months of audit logs and token access records; for anything beyond that we can work through our compliance pack.
- Air-gap rollback: yes — we support a manual pin-and-failover procedure. During the blackout test, the runtime stays active on pinned weights; if KV cache corruption is detected we have an automated cold-start that reinitializes the runtime from a verified snapshot. We’ll document the manual operator steps (we’ve added a rollback appendix to the test plan).
- Control-plane telemetry: no periodic checks to third-party registries are required for normal runtime. Any optional registry sync is an opt-in admin operation and can be disabled entirely for an air-gapped deployment. VendorX’s approach (you described) sounds like the exact pattern our infra flagged as higher risk.

Proposed kickoff: Thu, Sep 25, 9am PT — if that works, I’ll send a calendar invite and lock the technical runbook owners.

Related links: HubSpot record (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/FinOptima) — Ben will upload the artifacts there.

Attachments uploaded: FinOptima_PoC_TestPlan.xlsx (rev A), redwood-network-topology-draft.png, FinOptima_MutualActionPlan.pdf

Thanks — we’ll be ready to run the first control-plane handshake test during the kickoff.

—
